aboutPage.metaDescription: About the AI tool for indie developers that turns a README or GitHub repository into marketing posts for X.
aboutPage.headlineLine2: and get 5 draft posts for X.
aboutPage.lead: Paste a repository URL and Code Tweet loads the README automatically, then generates five posts — intro, how-to, use case, relatable, and CTA — each with a suggested posting time.
aboutPage.step1Body: Paste https://github.com/owner/repo into the input. Code Tweet fetches the README for you, so there's no need to copy the text yourself. Only when a repository has no README do you paste a description directly.
aboutPage.step2Body: Fill these in only if you want to set the tone, the URL to announce, or hashtags. You can skip all of them and still get 5 posts.
aboutPage.step3Body: All five posts — intro, how-to, use case, relatable, and CTA — arrive at once with suggested posting times. The "Post on X" button opens X's composer with the text already in place (you can also just copy it).
aboutPage.stepsHint: Tip: sign in with GitHub to unlock the "Choose a repository" button, which lists your public repositories. No more copying URLs every time.
aboutPage.feature1Body: Paste a URL and the README is fetched from the repository and previewed. No copy-pasting the text yourself.
aboutPage.feature2Body: Five posts in order — intro, how-to, use case, relatable, CTA — each playing a different role.
aboutPage.feature3Body: Within the next 7 days, it suggests a weekday and time that suits each post — and explains why.
aboutPage.feature4Body: Weighted length is calculated with twitter-text, and anything over the limit is flagged in red.
aboutPage.feature5Title: Post to X in one click
aboutPage.feature5Body: The "Post on X" button opens X's composer with your text already filled in — no copy-and-paste needed.
aboutPage.sampleText:
Just shipped Code Tweet, a side project of mine.

Paste a GitHub README and it drafts 5 posts for X in one go.

I built it to fix that gap where the code is done but the announcements never keep up.
aboutPage.sampleReason: Weekday evenings are when indie developers check X. Ideal for announcing something new.
aboutPage.quotaBody: After signing in with GitHub, Code Tweet is free for 3 generations a month. Need more? Top up with a credit pack (from 10 generations for ¥100). Purchased credits never expire.

aboutNotePage.metaDescription: Generates Markdown structured for note.com's syntax and audience. Title length, body length, formatting, and link placement are validated and regenerated by the tool rather than left to the AI.
aboutNotePage.lead: Generates Markdown structured for note.com's syntax and audience. Title length, body length, formatting, and link placement are validated and regenerated by the tool rather than left to the AI.
aboutNotePage.ctaQuality: What we do automatically for quality ↓
aboutNotePage.sectionQuality: What we do automatically for quality
aboutNotePage.qualityLead: Constraints the tool applies so "AI-generated" doesn't mean "sloppy" — and so you have less to fix by hand.
aboutNotePage.step1Body: Paste https://github.com/owner/repo into the input. The README is fetched automatically.
aboutNotePage.step2Body: Choose short (2–3 min), standard (4–6 min), or long (7–10 min). You can optionally add a tone, an announcement URL, and hashtags.
aboutNotePage.step3Body: You get a title, a six-section Markdown body, and hashtags. Just copy and paste into note.com.
aboutNotePage.quality1Body: If the AI returns a title longer than 32 characters, the tool detects it and asks for a regeneration — guaranteeing the title won't be truncated in note.com's title field.
aboutNotePage.quality2Title: Double-checks both minimum and maximum length
aboutNotePage.quality2Body: If the result falls outside the preset you chose (short 600–1,200 / standard 1,500–2,200 / long 2,500–3,500 characters), it's regenerated. This mechanically prevents both "too short to say anything" and "too long to read".
aboutNotePage.quality3Body: Strips syntax note.com doesn't support (Markdown links, code blocks, tables, and so on) from the AI's Markdown, leaving only headings (##), bold (**), and lists (- / 1.). Pasting is all it takes — the conversion happens automatically.
aboutNotePage.quality4Title: The URL appears once, in the closing section
aboutNotePage.quality4Body: To stop the same URL repeating through the body, the link you provide is placed once, in the closing section. It's a constraint that keeps the article from reading as spam.

aboutAppssPage.metaDescription: Build App Store screenshots — the ads that decide whether people download — from your GitHub README, with AI. Copy generation, AI-picked themes and backgrounds, highlighted keywords, and one-shot export in every required size, all in the browser.
aboutAppssPage.headlineLine2: as ads — and build them with AI.
aboutAppssPage.lead: Hand over your GitHub README and AI proposes the headline copy, layout, and color scheme for your App Store screenshots. All that's left is dropping in your app's screens and exporting. Everything happens in the browser.
aboutAppssPage.whyHeadingLine2Before: just pictures of your app — they're
aboutAppssPage.whyBody1: The screenshots you upload to App Store Connect aren't just pictures of your app. They're the single most important marketing asset you have — the thing a visitor uses to decide, in a few seconds, whether to download.
aboutAppssPage.whyBody2: So instead of listing features, you need to sell the value people get — in words that land and a design that stands out. App SS is a tool for building that ad together with AI. Even as a solo developer, you can put together screenshots as persuasive as the top charts', in very little time.
aboutAppssPage.step1Body: Enter https://github.com/owner/repo, or sign in and pick a repository. The README is fetched automatically.
aboutAppssPage.step2Body: Use the extra prompt for the writing style (soft, premium, and so on) and the theme for the color scheme. Leave either on "Let AI choose" and it's picked from your app's content.
aboutAppssPage.step3Title: Generate, drop in your images, export
aboutAppssPage.step3Body: AI produces the headline copy and layout in one pass. Drop your own app screenshots into the editor, then export every required App Store size (6.9–6.1 inch) as PNGs in one go.
aboutAppssPage.sampleLead: An example built for a fictional app. Headline copy, highlighted words, colors, background, and device frame are all export-ready as shown — you only swap in your own app's screens.
aboutAppssPage.demoAlt1: App SS sample output: hero layout
aboutAppssPage.demoAlt2: App SS sample output: feature layout
aboutAppssPage.demoAlt3: App SS sample output: progress layout
aboutAppssPage.feature1Title: AI writes headline copy from your README
aboutAppssPage.feature1Body: Instead of listing features, AI writes headlines around the change users get — the way top App Store apps do it. Note: generated copy is currently Japanese.
aboutAppssPage.feature2Body: Pick from 11 ready-made themes, or let AI generate a bespoke palette that matches your app's feel each time. It also suggests one of 5 background treatments — and you can always override it by hand.
aboutAppssPage.feature3Body: AI picks the word that lands hardest in each headline and sets it in the accent color — the single-word emphasis that professional store ads rely on, done for you.
aboutAppssPage.feature4Body: Screenshots you import are stored only in the browser (IndexedDB), so you can safely work with screens from an unreleased app.
aboutAppssPage.feature5Body: Nine Japanese typefaces — gothic, rounded, mincho and more — with the fonts embedded in the exported images, so Japanese text really looks the part.
aboutAppssPage.feature6Title: Export every App Store size at once
aboutAppssPage.feature6Body: Export 6.9 / 6.5 / 6.3 / 6.1 inch as PNGs in a single pass, ready to upload straight to App Store Connect.

After signing in with GitHub, it's free for 3 generations a month; top up with a credit pack (from 10 generations for ¥100) if you need more. privacyPage.metaDescription: What information Code Tweet collects, why it is used, and which external services are involved.
privacyPage.heading: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.lead: This page explains what information Code Tweet handles, why it is used, what is sent to external services, and how to delete it.
privacyPage.s1Body: Code Tweet handles: the email address from your GitHub sign-in, GitHub account identifiers, the connection details needed to fetch your GitHub README and repository list, your generation count, plan determination, usage logs, and a hashed form of your IP address when you use the service as a guest. From GitHub we retrieve only README files and repository listing information (name, description, public/private status, updated time, and the like) — we never retrieve, view, or store source code. We also handle the project description, README, extra prompt, URL, and hashtags you enter when generating posts. For credit purchasers and subscribers, the generation history we store consists of the generated posts, suggested posting times, URLs, hashtags, and generation timestamps; the README body and extra prompt body are not stored. Generation history is kept to the 50 most recent entries per user, and older entries beyond that are deleted automatically when new ones are added.
privacyPage.s2Body: We use the information we collect to verify your sign-in status, enforce usage limits, determine your plan, fetch your GitHub README and repository list, generate posts with AI, prevent abuse, respond to enquiries, and improve the service.
privacyPage.s3Body: We use a GitHub App to fetch READMEs from private repositories. The granted permission is limited to Contents: Read-only, which GitHub enforces. This service does not store per-user access tokens. When a README needs to be fetched, the server issues a single-use access token that expires automatically after about an hour, and discards it after use. The only thing kept in the database is the installation identifier (a number), which on its own cannot access any repository. You can revoke the connection at any time from GitHub under Settings → Applications → Installed GitHub Apps.
privacyPage.s4Body: When posts are generated, the project description, README, extra prompt, URL, hashtags, and similar input you provide are sent to the Google Gemini API. Do not include private keys, access tokens, passwords, third parties' personal information, or unpublished confidential information in your README or prompts.
privacyPage.s5Body: This service uses Supabase for authentication and its database, GitHub for sign-in and repository information, the Google Gemini API for post generation, Vercel for hosting, runtime, and usage analytics (Vercel Analytics / Vercel Speed Insights), Google Analytics provided by Google LLC for access analysis, and Microsoft Clarity for UX improvement via heatmaps and session recordings. How each external service handles information is governed by its own privacy policy and terms of service.
privacyPage.s6Body: We use the following analytics tools to improve the service and detect faults. Vercel Analytics uses no cookies and collects anonymous page views, referrers, region, and device information. Vercel Speed Insights collects performance metrics such as LCP, CLS, and INP. Google Analytics uses cookies to measure access patterns including page views, referrers, region, and device information (IP addresses are anonymized by Google). If you wish to opt out of measurement by Google Analytics, you can use Google's "Google Analytics Opt-out Browser Add-on" (https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout). Microsoft Clarity uses cookies for heatmaps and session recordings, capturing on-page interactions (clicks, scrolling, mouse movement) in anonymized form. Password fields, credit card details, and other sensitive input fields are masked automatically and are never recorded in plain text.
privacyPage.s7Body: Signed-in users can delete their account from the settings page. Deletion removes information tied to you, including your account, GitHub connection details, usage history, generation history, and plan information. Some logs or information may nonetheless remain for a period of time due to legal compliance, abuse prevention, incident investigation, or the retention behaviour of external services.
privacyPage.s8Body: Secrets such as API keys, the GitHub App private key, and the Service Role Key are managed as server-side environment variables and are never exposed to the client. IP addresses from guest usage are stored in hashed form. Access to private repositories uses short-lived GitHub App tokens, and no per-user access tokens are stored. Access rights are controlled based on authentication state and user ID.
privacyPage.s9Body: For enquiries about the handling, deletion, correction, or suspension of use of personal information, please contact us through the contact page. Where identity verification is required, we will respond after confirming your sign-in status and registered details.
privacyPage.s10Body: This policy may be updated as the service or the external services it uses change. Significant changes will be announced within the service.
privacyPage.s11Body: The code this service uses to communicate with GitHub (fetching READMEs and repository listings) is published so that third parties can verify it. The only GitHub APIs called are those for fetching a README and listing repositories; no API that retrieves source code is used.
privacyPage.s11Link: Review the GitHub communication code (on GitHub)

settingsPage.metaDescription: Check your Code Tweet credit balance and GitHub connection status.

settingsPage.usageNote: Once your monthly free allowance runs out, purchased credits are spent one at a time. Credits never expire.

settingsPage.freeLimits: README limit of {limit} characters, public repositories only (buy credits for {paid} characters, history, and private repositories)

settingsForm.deleteNetworkError: Failed to delete your account. Please check your connection and try again.
settingsForm.deleteBody1: This deletes your account, GitHub connection, usage history, generation history, and plan information.
settingsForm.deleteBody2: Any unused purchased credits are deleted too — they can't be restored or refunded. This action can't be undone.
settingsForm.blockedTitle: You can't delete your account while a subscription is active
settingsForm.blockedBody: Cancel your subscription first from the Stripe customer portal. Once Stripe confirms the cancellation, you'll be able to delete your account here (it may take a moment to take effect).
settingsForm.confirmBody: This is a final check against accidental deletion. Once you proceed, your account and its data can't be recovered.
settingsForm.confirmScope: Includes: your account, GitHub connection, usage history, generation history, plan information, and remaining purchased credits (non-refundable)
settingsForm.privateRepoBody: Buy credits and Code Tweet can also fetch READMEs from your private repositories via the GitHub connection, letting you pick them from the repository list.
settingsForm.afterPurchase: After purchasing, you can set up the private repository connection on this page.
settingsForm.githubAppBody1: Used to fetch READMEs from private repositories. We don't store access tokens — the server issues a single-use token that expires in about an hour. The only permission granted is
settingsForm.githubAppBody2: — we never retrieve the contents of your repositories (your source code).
settingsForm.installIntro: Pressing "Connect GitHub" opens GitHub's installation screen.
settingsForm.installStep1a: Choose which repositories to allow with
settingsForm.installStep2b: only — set automatically and enforced by GitHub
settingsForm.installStep3: Press "Install" and you'll return here, connected
settingsForm.revokeNote: You can revoke the connection any time on GitHub: Settings → Applications → Installed GitHub Apps → Uninstall.
settingsForm.notConfigured: The GitHub App connection isn't set up yet. Please hold tight until it's ready.
